  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, May 23, 2023  7:00 PM  Council Chambers

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO AVALON ROOFING INC.

  BUILDINGS
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Public Works Director
  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to enter into a Public Works
  Contract with Avalon Roofing Inc. (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to
  replace the roofs on the City Hall and Council Chambers buildings, in the amount of

  CODE

  Attachments: Staff Report + Ordinance No. 747

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 23, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR HUFF at 7:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Scouts Earth Day Art Contest winners Savanna Winters, Chloe Paik, and Heidi
Screen.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF EARTH DAY ART CONTEST WINNERS

MAYOR HUFF presented Savanna Winters, Chloe Paik and Heidi Screen with Certificates of
Recognition as winners of the 2023 Earth Day Art contest.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DOORS OPEN PENINSULA

MAYOR HUFF declared June 17, 223 as Doors Open Peninsula Day, and presented the
proclamation to Palos Verdes Library District (PVLD) Director Jennifer Addington, PVLD
President Rosa Quan Easton, PVLD Vice-President Bob Park and PVLD Trustee Jonathan
Beutler.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-G AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MAY 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66249 THROUGH 66265 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $31,790.25, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050123 THROUGH
  050423; IN THE AMOUNT OF $118,980.23 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $150,770.48 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 23, 2023
 C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF MAY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF MAY 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS & TRANSFER FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 9, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 1, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE - SECOND QUARTER 2023

Erick Quintero, Waste Management Public Sector Services Manager, presented the
following winners of Waste Management’s 2nd quarter Recycling Hero drawing:

  COMMERCIAL WINNER: NEW HORIZONS CHILD DEVELOPMENT CENTER
  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 13 HILLCREST MEADOWS

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO AVALON ROOFING INC. TO RE-
  ROOF CITY HALL AND THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS BUILDINGS

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to enter into a Public Works
  Contract with Avalon Roofing Inc. (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to
  replace the roofs on the City Hall and Council Chambers buildings, in the amount of
  $131,475, plus a $20,000 contingency, which includes permit and inspection services
  by Willdan Engineering, for a grand total of $151,475.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed with staff that the roof material is fire retardant. She
also confirmed references were checked for Avalon Roofing Inc.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed concern about the $20,000 contingency being too
low. Staff explained that additional funds could be added under the City Manager’s signing limit
if needed, in an effort to not delay the project.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 23, 2023
   DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER INTO A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH
  AVALON ROOFING INC. (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY), TO REPLACE THE ROOFS ON THE CITY HALL AND COUNCIL
  CHAMBERS BUILDINGS, IN THE AMOUNT OF $131,475, PLUS A $20,000
  CONTINGENCY, WHICH INCLUDES PERMIT AND INSPECTION SERVICES
  BY WILLDAN ENGINEERING, FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $151,475.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  WASTE MANAGEMENT REQUEST FOR RATE ADJUSTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Waste Management’s request for a
  rate adjustment on all levels of service as included in the attached FY 2023-24
  Collection Service Rate Schedule effective July 1, 2023.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the rate change is not correlated with the proposed
schedule change, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE WASTE MANAGEMENT’S REQUEST FOR A RATE
  ADJUSTMENT ON ALL LEVELS OF SERVICE AS INCLUDED IN THE FY
  2023-24 COLLECTION SERVICE RATE SCHEDULE EFFECTIVE JULY 1,
  2023.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PROJECT LIST FOR SB 1 FUND ELIGIBILITY; FISCAL YEAR 2023-24
  (RESOLUTION NO. 2545)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2545, adopting a list
  of projects for Fiscal Year 2023-24 funded by SB 1, the Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2545, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 FUNDED BY SB 1, THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2545 by title.

D.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement per City Attorney’s
  approval and rates for the CPA firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to
  perform the annual audit and report for the Fiscal Year 2022-23, perform the single
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 23, 2023
   audit if needed, prepare the Pepper Tree Foundation’s tax returns, and review the
  GANN appropriation limitation.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE AGREEMENT PER CITY ATTORNEY’S APPROVAL AND
  RATES FOR THE CPA FIRM OF ROGERS, ANDERSON, MALODY & SCOTT,
  LLP TO PERFORM THE ANNUAL AUDIT AND REPORT FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2022-23, PERFORM THE SINGLE AUDIT IF NEEDED, PREPARE THE
  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S TAX RETURNS, AND REVIEW THE GANN
  APPROPRIATION LIMITATION.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 746 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 6.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO ANIMAL REGULATIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 746.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  CONDUCT THE SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 746.

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 746 by title.

B.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 747 TO ADD CHAPTER
  8.42 (SINGLE-USE FOODWARE ACCESSORIES) TO TITLE 8 (HEALTH AND
  SAFETY) OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Find that Ordinance No. 747 is exempt from
  the provisions of CEQA, per Section 15060(c)(2) and Section 15060(c)(3), because the
  subject ordinance and regulations have no potential for resulting in any significant
  physical change to the environment, either directly or indirectly; and 2) Conduct the
  second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 747.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material.)

Community Development Director Naughton explained the compliance procedures outlined in
the municipal code, as well as staff’s educational plan for this ordinance, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 23, 2023
   COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  FIND THAT ORDINANCE NO. 747 IS EXEMPT FROM THE PROVISIONS OF
  CEQA, PER SECTION 15060(C)(2) AND SECTION 15060(C)(3), BECAUSE
  THE SUBJECT ORDINANCE AND REGULATIONS HAVE NO POTENTIAL
  FOR RESULTING IN ANY SIGNIFICANT PHYSICAL CHANGE TO THE
  ENVIRONMENT, EITHER DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY; AND CONDUCT THE
  SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 747.

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 747 by title.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR HUFF attended the California Contract Cities Association’s Annual Municipal Seminar
with COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA will be attending the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) Board of Directors meeting Thursday.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR HUFF reported on the successful Mayor’s Ride event held May 13.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Potential initiation of litigation: one case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:45 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Planning
Commissioner and longtime Rolling Hills Estates resident Joan Friedman. Meeting
adjourned to Tuesday, May 30, 2023, at 12:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Budget Workshop.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 23, 2023
